feature: Shift Command J closes an open path
summary: With one open outline picked and no marquee up, Shift Command J now closes it on its own two ends. With a marquee up the key is still Photoshop's New Layer via Cut, and the menu bar prints the key on whichever of the two rows it will run.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/shift-command-j-closes-a-path-walk.json (it brings the probe to the front, so it waits for nobody to be at the Mac).

try.do: Press P, click three points of a triangle, press Return, then Escape. Pick the Path row.
Open the Layer menu: Shift Command J sits beside Close Path…, and New Layer via Cut shows no key.
Press Shift Command J and answer Close Path in the question.
Look at the canvas: the third side is there, the notice says Closed, and the Fill row has appeared.
Press Command Z once: the outline is open again.
Drop a screenshot, marquee a word on it, and open the Layer menu: Shift Command J is back on New Layer via Cut.
Press Shift Command J: the word lifts onto a layer of its own, as before.

evaluate: Does a key that changes rows depending on whether a marquee is up feel natural, or surprising?
Should the key close the path straight away instead of asking the question first, the way Illustrator's Join does?
Would you expect Shift Command J to close the path while you are still drawing it with the Pen, before pressing Return?
rough: The key runs the same row as the menu, so it asks the Close this path question every time until Don't ask again is ticked; Illustrator closes with no question.

The mock (vector-wt.html, Path inspector step) also puts a Close path button in the panel; whether the panel keeps one-shot buttons is the open card the-panel-shows-what-the-picked-thing-is-and-its-how-many-buttons-may-the-right-h.
The Layer menu's Close Path… with Shift Command J matches the mock's command popover, which prints the same pair.
Shift Command J does nothing while the Pen is still drawing; you finish with Return or Escape first.
